messages:
sam: quick async check — small status thread for api v2 compatibility work. I want a concise green/red on the pieces below by EOD: SDK patch, router shim, telemetry tags, and canary window. no meeting unless we need it.

alice: SDK patch (js/python) is built and passing unit tests, still running integ tests against our internal dev cluster. i'll link the PR in a sec.

ben: telemetry instrumentation is only partial — request id + route tag added but not model_variant. we need model_variant in traces for A/B comparison during canary. cc @eng-ml for model tagging schema.

carol: canary window proposed: tomorrow 09:00-11:00 PST, 5% traffic -> 25% step. fallback policy is in place to route to v1. canary deployment manifest is uploaded to ci:refs/canary/slot-7.

sam: @carol thanks. can you paste the flag key/name we use for gating? want to wire the SDK so customers can opt-in if needed.

carol: sure — flag name is api_compat_v2_gated. example config: ```json
{"flags": {"api_compat_v2_gated": "on_by_default"}}
```

dana: ownership clarifier — who owns the reranker endpoint conversion? last I saw it was tentatively eng-ml but infra had to add a proxy shim. we should lock a single owner before canary.

alice: reranker: eng-ml owns model conversion and tests, eng-platform owns the shim and rollout automation. i've added a small checklist in the PR describing handoff steps.

ben: small ask: please ensure SDKs include a clear deprecation warning when a user hits the v1 endpoint after the flag toggles. minimal text is fine, but should include migration guide link.

sam: noted. @alice can you add that text to the SDK changelog and code? wording: "v1 endpoints deprecated — see /docs/migrate-api-v2 for guidance."

alice: will do, adding to the patch.

deploy-bot: Canary build queued: slot-7 -> start at 1712352000. status: queued (operator: carol).

carol: small snag — dev cluster reported an ephemeral SSL mismatch for the shim in staging. i scheduled a short maintenance 08:30 PST to refresh certs; this may push canary back by ~15m.

sam: ok — please update this thread when certs are refreshed. if it slips more than 30m, we reschedule to next day same window.

dana: quick question on telemetry retention for the canary traces: do we keep them 90 days by default or shorter? we might want longer to compare across traffic slices.

ben: ops default is 30 days, but we can request extended retention per-run. eng-sre + finance need to approve extended retention due to cost. i can open the ticket now if you want.

sam: open the ticket and ping finance; mark it high priority. final ask: please confirm readiness (green/red) for your area in this thread before EOD. thanks everyone.
